hyp: Tteokbokki is chewy rice cakes and fish cake simmered in a thick wheat chili sauce, a street food favorite. Be warned, it's properly spicy, so ask for a milder version if you're not used to heat. Eat it straight from the pan while it's hot using a fork or a toothpick. It has gluten and soy in it. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

nakji bokkeum is fresh octopus soft fried with vegetables fiercely chewy seriously hot this one is very spicy go carefully if you're not used to eat it with rice to take edge off and keep a cold drink nearby it has octopus and soy in it so it's out if you avoid seafood this is general info not medical advice check with the restaurant about allergies

아귀찜 is monkfish and bean sprouts braised together in a thick garlicky chili sauce meant for sharing. It's very spicy, so pace yourself. Everyone eats from the middle of the table. Use your chopsticks to pick out the fish and sprouts. It has fish and soy in it, so it's out if you avoid seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Maeuntang is a fiery fish stew, often made from what's left after with radish. It's very spicy. There's a lot of chili in that broth. Eat it hot with rice, pruning up both the fish and the broth. It has fish and soy in it, so it's out if you avoid seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bibimbap is a bowl of warm rice piled with seasoned vegetables, beef, and a fried egg. The Korean chili paste makes it mildly spicy, but you can ask for less. Give it a good mix with your spoon before you dig in. It has egg and soy, and most places do a meat-free version if you ask. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Bulgogi is thin slices of beef marinated in sweet soy sauce with garlic and sesame oil, then grilled until tender. There's no heat to it at all. It's sweet and savory. Eat it straight with rice or wrap a piece in lettuce with garlic. It has soy and sesame in it, and the soy sauce may bring gluten. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Kimchi jjigae is a bubbling stew of aged kimchi, pork, and tofu in a tangy broth. The kimchi and chili flakes give it a solid kick. It comes in a shared pot, so ladle some into your own bowl and eat it with rice. It has soy in it, the broth sometimes has fish or seafood, and the pork version isn't halal or kosher. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

된장찌개 is a hearty stew of fermented soybean paste with tofu, zucchini, potato, and mushrooms. It isn't spicy at all, deep and savory, a little funky from the fermentation. Eat it hot, spooning both the broth and the vegetables over rice. It has soy in it, and it's vegetarian if the stock has no meat or seafood. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with a restaurant about allergies.

Samgyeopsal is thick slices of plain pork belly that you grill yourself at the table. The meat isn't spicy though the dipping paste that comes with it is. Wrap a slice in a lettuce leaf with garlic and a dab of that paste. It has soy in it and it's pork so skip it if you avoid either. This is general info not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergies.

Galbitang is beef short ribs simmered slowly into a clear soup with radish and glass noodles. There's no heat at all. Just a light, savory broth seasoned with salt and garlic. Pull the tender meat off the ribs with your spoon and sip the broth as you go. It's mostly free of common allergens, but the soy sauce is worth asking about. This is general info, not medical advice. Check with the restaurant about allergens.
